draft.title: Conditional probability
card: Pr(A | B) is the probability of A given that B has happened. Knowing B has happened shrinks the sample space to just the outcomes in B.
Formula: Pr(A | B) = Pr(A ∩ B)/Pr(B). The bottom is the event we are given. The top is the part of it that is also A.
From a table, Pr(A | B) = (number in both A and B) ÷ (number in B). Use only the row or column for B as the total.
Example: in a class of 30, 12 play netball, and 8 of those 12 also play tennis. Pr(tennis | netball) = 8/12 = 2/3. The total is 12, not 30.
draft.remember: Given B means B is the new total. Divide by Pr(B), not by everything.

a.q: For two events, Pr(A ∩ B) = 0.2 and Pr(B) = 0.5. Find Pr(A | B).
a.why: Pr(A | B) = Pr(A ∩ B) ÷ Pr(B) = 0.2 ÷ 0.5 = 0.4. Multiplying gives 0.1, but the formula divides by the probability of the given event.
a.clue: The event after the bar goes on the bottom.

b.q: At a school camp, 40 students chose activities. 25 chose kayaking, and 10 of those also chose archery. 5 chose only archery. One archery student is picked at random. What is the probability they also chose kayaking?
b.why: Archery has 10 + 5 = 15 students, and 10 of them chose kayaking, so the probability is 10/15 = 2/3. The option 2/5 is 10/25, which divides by the kayakers and so reverses the condition. The given event is archery, so it goes on the bottom.
b.clue: Find the total number who chose archery first.

final.title: Conditional probability
card: \(\text{Pr}(A \mid B)\) is the probability of \(A\) given that \(B\) has happened. Knowing \(B\) has happened shrinks the sample space to just the outcomes in \(B\).
Formula: \(\text{Pr}(A \mid B) = \frac{\text{Pr}(A \cap B)}{\text{Pr}(B)}\). The bottom is the event we are given. The top is the part of it that is also \(A\).
From a table, \(\text{Pr}(A \mid B)\) is the number in both \(A\) and \(B\), divided by the number in \(B\). Use only the row or column for \(B\) as the total.
Example: in a class of 30, 12 play netball, and 8 of those 12 also play tennis. \(\text{Pr}(\text{tennis} \mid \text{netball}) = \frac{8}{12} = \frac{2}{3}\). The total is 12, not 30.
final.remember: Given \(B\) means \(B\) is the new total. Divide by \(\text{Pr}(B)\), not by everything.

a.q: For two events, \(\text{Pr}(A \cap B) = 0.2\) and \(\text{Pr}(B) = 0.5\). Find \(\text{Pr}(A \mid B)\).
a.why: \(\text{Pr}(A \mid B) = \text{Pr}(A \cap B) \div \text{Pr}(B)\), which is \(0.2 \div 0.5 = 0.4\). Multiplying gives 0.1, but the formula divides by the probability of the given event.
a.clue: The event after the bar goes on the bottom.

b.q: At a school camp, 40 students chose activities. 25 chose kayaking, and 10 of those also chose archery. 5 chose only archery. One archery student is picked at random. What is the probability they also chose kayaking?
b.why: Archery has \(10 + 5 = 15\) students, and 10 of them chose kayaking, so the probability is \(\frac{10}{15} = \frac{2}{3}\). The option \(\frac{2}{5}\) is \(\frac{10}{25}\), which divides by the kayakers and so reverses the condition. The given event is archery, so it goes on the bottom.
b.clue: Find the total number who chose archery first.
